items.name: Desert wall map: poster board, markers, flag pins
items.why: Twelve waypoints, the crossing mornings and the two far stars with their real dates. Dates, never counts.

items.name: Expedition dossier board: poster board and markers
items.why: Started in week 1 and built up all season: the motion bank, the through-line, the guest list with a job beside every name, and the run of show with minutes added at the bottom.

items.name: g++ toolchain and an editor on the Windows laptop (MinGW-w64 or WSL), installed and verified by a grown-up before week 1
items.why: The entire Build track this season. Free, and installing it before the season is what keeps week 1's Build hour honest.

items.name: Jumbo sidewalk chalk
items.why: Konigsberg drawn on the driveway and walked on foot, and the week 1 line walked on a chalk grid.

items.name: Min-max outdoor thermometer
items.why: The thirty second dawn temperature log, which becomes their own statistics data in week 9, gaps and all.

items.name: Stopwatch showing tenths of a second, on a phone or a kitchen timer
items.why: The week 3 race: two languages timed on the same loop by their own hand, and the gap written down as a measured number. Household, no spend.

items.name: Analog desk clock, and no phone on the desk
items.why: They manage the crossing morning's clock themselves, and a clock they have to remember to check is a clock that is checking on them. It becomes part of their own protocol card in week 7.

items.name: Planisphere or star wheel, set for your latitude
items.why: The week 7 star night after scientific notation: the zoom lever taken outside and pointed at real distances. The cheapest field trip in the season, and it keeps working every clear night afterwards.

items.name: Stiff index cards and a pen that does not smudge
items.why: The protocol card they write in week 7 and revises at the week 8 oasis. It has to survive a four or five hour morning on a desk and a pocket afterwards, which is why it is a card and not a page.

items.name: Time capsule: two heavy envelopes
items.why: Written and sealed at the week 8 oasis, with each envelope's opening date inked on the front, and stored where the family agrees they can be found again.

items.name: Two-pan balance scale, or a coat hanger, string and two paper cups, plus twelve matching coins
items.why: Month 3's monster deserves real hands. Building the balance out of a hanger is part of the puzzle rather than a chore before it, and the same twelve coins get performed for the family at the Grand Expedition.

items.name: Two official USACO solution pages, printed on paper with wide margins, and a coloured pen
items.why: The maintenance week's reading job. Annotating happens in the margins of paper, not in a browser tab, and the two pages are the analyses for problems they have already beaten themselves. Free to print.

items.name: Fresh batteries for the season 1 badge and the mBot
items.why: Wakes the old badge circuit and the mBot creature for one more run at the Grand Expedition finale, both idle since season 2.

items.name: Grand Expedition day kit: printed invitations, station props, shade and water, a modest spread, the fourth terrain patch and the arc patch
items.why: Week 12 is a produced event with real guests, and the production starts in week 11, when the invitations are actually sent rather than mentioned. Needed by week 11 so that the invitations exist to send.

items.name: Phone tripod or stand
items.why: Keeps the finale recording steady instead of propped and drifting.

items.name: Extension cord
items.why: Powers the laptop at the finale table without the cord underfoot or a wobble by the screen.

items.name: Field Atlas: an archival binder or a bookbinding kit, plus photo prints and printouts
items.why: The bound keep-forever portfolio, closed at the Grand Expedition with the time capsule sealed inside it. Originals are never destroyed; the Atlas takes copies wherever a copy will do.

items.name: Paper and a pencil for Sprouts
items.why: The season 4 sprint 1 game, needed by week 1.

items.name: Blokus set
items.why: The season 4 sprint 2 game, needed by week 5.

items.name: Quarto set
items.why: The season 4 sprint 3 game, needed by week 9.

items.name: Arduino IDE and ESP32 board support (free software install, at https://www.arduino.cc)
items.why: Installed and verified by a grown-up before week 1, so the season's first hour is spent measuring the loop instead of fighting a board-manager install.

items.name: Two ESP32 dev boards
items.why: Says hello and measures loop time in week 1, then talks to its own twin over ESP-NOW in that same merged week. Binds a receiver to a real flight controller from week 2, and from week 11 sends the Mars rover and arm their delayed commands.

items.name: Cheap digital temperature probe
items.why: Takes the repeated point-in-time readings for week 5's cooling extra, alongside the arm and gripper build. The min-max thermometer only records extremes, not a time series.

items.name: Small solar cell
items.why: Measured at different tilt angles and under simulated dust as week 6's extra, alongside the walker. The rover's own power still comes from its battery, not the sun.

items.name: 74HC00 and 74HC86 chips
items.why: Replaces the season 2 copper gates with a real NAND chip in week 9, then rebuilds the adder from both chips in week 10.

items.name: Battery-powered AM radio
items.why: Tuned to a gap of static and held near the week 10 ring oscillator, it reveals the ring switching by ear, since the ring's real frequency is far too fast for the multimeter to see directly.

items.name: Small strong magnet
items.why: Checks whether a rusted screw still pulls to a magnet the same way a clean one does.

items.name: Flight controller with integrated 4-in-1 ESCs (whoop or toothpick class, Betaflight-compatible), receiver and a radio transmitter
items.why: Turns the season 3 bench-tested quad frame into a flyable aircraft. A real flight controller reads the receiver and corrects the quad's tilt hundreds of times a second. The transmitter is the child's own hands on the stick for the first tethered and free hovers.

items.name: Programmable SDK drone (Tello EDU class)
items.why: A reference aircraft with a documented text-command SDK. Fly it through a coded square and measure how far dead reckoning lets it drift from a taped square on the floor.

items.name: Eight metal-gear hobby servos (MG90S class, about 2.2 kg-cm stall torque) and a 16-channel servo driver board (PCA9685 class)
items.why: Builds the 3 degree-of-freedom arm, 3 servos, in week 5. It also builds the four-legged walker, up to eight servos, two joints per leg, in weeks 6 and 7. The driver board frees the ESP32 from timing every pulse itself.

items.name: Pressure and temperature sensor breakout (BMP280 or BME280 class) for the ESP32 payload
items.why: The flying payload's instrument: logs pressure and temperature under the quad in the week 2 extra, and height is read from the pressure drop.

items.name: Software-defined radio dongle (RTL-SDR v4 class) with a V-dipole antenna kit
items.why: Receives a real weather satellite's picture in the week 11 extra: the first time a satellite talks to something he built. The dongle also hears aircraft and amateur radio for later.
